User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account in the application, distinguishing between player and organization managers. It links to either a PlayerProfile or an OrganizationProfile.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

userType.description: Indicates whether the user is an 'Org' manager or a 'Player'.

email.description: The user's email address, primarily for communication.

discordId.description: The user's Discord ID, used for communication and linking accounts.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

PlayerProfile.title: PlayerProfile
PlayerProfile.description: Detailed profile information for a player, including their in-game stats, preferences, and gameplay highlights. This profile is linked to a User entity.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PlayerProfile entity.

userId.description: Reference to the associated User entity. (Relationship: User 1:1 PlayerProfile)

experience.description: Description of the player's gaming experience and background.

povLinks.description: A list of named links to gameplay footage (POVs), such as YouTube or Google Drive links.

idealTeammateStrategy.description: A detailed description of the player's ideal teammates and desired playstyle for synergy matching (e.g., 'I need an IGL who plays center-zone').

device.description: The mobile device operating system the player uses (e.g., iOS, Android).

profilePictureUrl.description: URL for the player's profile picture.

achievements.description: A list of notable achievements or accolades of the player.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the player profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the player profile was last updated.

OrganizationProfile.title: OrganizationProfile
OrganizationProfile.description: Detailed profile information for an organization or team, including branding, recruitment preferences, and verified status. This profile is linked to a User entity.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OrganizationProfile entity.

userId.description: Reference to the associated User entity. (Relationship: User 1:1 OrganizationProfile)

name.description: The official name of the organization or team.

logoUrl.description: URL to the organization's logo image.

bannerUrl.description: URL for the organization's profile banner image.

socialLinks.description: An array of URLs to the organization's social media profiles.

achievements.description: A list of notable achievements or accolades of the organization.

teamStyle.description: A description of the organization's overall team playstyle and strategy (e.g., Edge-Player, Aggressive, Drop-Clashers).

description.description: A general description or mission statement of the organization.

isVerified.description: Indicates if the organization profile has been officially verified.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the organization profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the organization profile was last updated.

RosterSlot.title: RosterSlot
RosterSlot.description: Represents a single position or slot within an organization's 5-man roster, indicating its status and the player filling it if any.

id.description: Unique identifier for the RosterSlot entity.

organizationId.description: Reference to the OrganizationProfile this slot belongs to. (Relationship: OrganizationProfile 1:N RosterSlot)

organizationManagerUserId.description: Denormalized ID of the user who manages the organization, for security rules.

slotName.description: A descriptive name for the roster slot (e.g., 'IGL Slot', 'Entry Fragger 1').

status.description: The current status of the roster slot.

playerId.description: Reference to the PlayerProfile currently occupying this slot. Null if 'Vacant' or 'Open for Replacement'. (Relationship: RosterSlot 0:1 PlayerProfile)

requiredRole.description: The primary role expected for a player filling this specific slot.

requiredPlaystyle.description: The desired playstyle for a player filling this slot.

minFdRatio.description: The minimum F/D (Finish/Death) ratio required for a player to be eligible for this slot.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the roster slot was created/defined.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the roster slot was last updated.

TryoutRequest.title: TryoutRequest
TryoutRequest.description: Represents a formal request from an organization to a player for a tryout, or a player's application to an organization, facilitating the matchmaking process.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TryoutRequest entity.

organizationId.description: Reference to the OrganizationProfile sending or receiving the request. (Relationship: OrganizationProfile 1:N TryoutRequest)

playerId.description: Reference to the PlayerProfile sending or receiving the request. (Relationship: PlayerProfile 1:N TryoutRequest)

playerUserId.description: Denormalized ID of the user associated with the player profile, for security rules.

organizationManagerUserId.description: Denormalized ID of the user who manages the organization, for security rules.

status.description: The current status of the tryout request.

message.description: An optional message included with the tryout request or application.

sentBy.description: Indicates whether the request was sent by 'Org' or 'Player'.

sentAt.description: Timestamp when the tryout request was sent.

respondedAt.description: Timestamp when the tryout request was responded to (accepted/declined).

synergyScore.description: The calculated synergy match score between the player and organization at the time the request was made.

isReadByPlayer.description: Indicates if the player has viewed an incoming request. Used for notifications.

isReadByOrg.description: Indicates if the org manager has viewed an incoming application. Used for notifications.

mouGeneratedAt.description: Timestamp when the MoU was generated after the request was accepted.

mouPlayerConfirmedAt.description: Timestamp when the player confirmed the MoU.

mouOrgConfirmedAt.description: Timestamp when the organization confirmed the MoU.

definition.description: Stores core user authentication information and user type (Org or Player). This collection is private, with read/write access restricted to the authenticated user matching the document's userId.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, corresponding to Firebase Authentication's UID.

definition.description: Contains detailed profile information for a player. This collection is publicly readable for discovery by organizations but writable only by the owning user. Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence.

params.name: playerProfileId
params.description: The unique identifier for the player's profile.

definition.description: Contains detailed profile information for an organization. This collection is publicly readable for discovery by players but writable only by the owning organization manager. Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence.

params.name: organizationProfileId
params.description: The unique identifier for the organization's profile.

definition.description: Represents a slot within an organization's 5-man roster. Writable only by the organization manager. Includes denormalized 'organizationManagerUserId' (the userId of the Org's manager) for authorization independence.

params.name: rosterSlotId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific roster slot.

definition.description: Manages tryout requests between players and organizations. Writable only by the involved player or organization manager. Includes denormalized 'playerUserId' and 'organizationManagerUserId' for authorization independence.

params.name: tryoutRequestId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific tryout request.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore structure prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation. Each entity is placed in its own top-level collection, ensuring homogeneous security postures within collections and simplifying security rules.

**Authorization Independence:** This is achieved through strategic denormalization. For documents whose access depends on a 'parent' or related entity's owner, the owner's `userId` is explicitly copied into the document. For instance:
*   `PlayerProfile` documents will include the `userId` of the owning `User`.
*   `OrganizationProfile` documents will include the `userId` of the owning `User`.
*   `RosterSlot` documents, which are owned by an organization, will denormalize the `userId` of the `OrganizationProfile`'s manager (renamed to `organizationManagerUserId` for clarity) directly into the `RosterSlot` document. This allows rules to check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.organizationManagerUserId` without needing to perform a `get()` operation on the parent `OrganizationProfile` document.
*   `TryoutRequest` documents involve both a player and an organization. To allow both parties to manage the request independently, both the `userId` of the player (`playerUserId`) and the `userId` of the organization's manager (`organizationManagerUserId`) are denormalized into each `TryoutRequest` document. This eliminates complex `get()` calls and facilitates atomic updates.

**Support for Query-Aware Permissions (QAPs):** The structural segregation inherently supports QAPs by separating data with different access requirements:
*   `/player_profiles` and `/organization_profiles` collections are designed to be globally readable (for discovery by organizations and players, respectively) but write-restricted to their respective owners. This allows efficient `list` operations (e.g., 'show all players an Org can recruit', 'show all Orgs a player can apply to') without needing complex rule-based filtering, as the read permission is broad and the write permission is specific.
*   `/roster_slots` and `/tryout_requests` collections contain data that is private to the involved parties. By denormalizing the owner `userId`s, `list` operations on these collections can efficiently filter by `userId` (e.g., `db.collection('roster_slots').where('organizationManagerUserId', '==', currentUser.uid)`) and security rules can strictly enforce that only the `currentUser.uid` can access their specific documents.

This design minimizes rule complexity, prevents waterfall `get()` operations, and ensures that data integrity and security are maintained efficiently across all read and write operations.
